summary_short: e.l.f. Beauty's quarter ended March 31, 2026 revenue was $449M (+35.1% y/y, -8.2% q/q), but the quarter swung to a $49M net loss (diluted EPS -$0.82) versus profits in both the prior quarter and year-ago quarter.
summary_long: For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (which this quarter closes), net sales grew 25% to $1.64B; rhode (acquired August 2025) added $293.5M, pricing/mix added $333.5M, partly offset by $10.5M lower volume. Full-year gross margin slipped ~50bp to 70.7% on tariffs, partly offset by pricing. SG&A rose 32% on marketing, compensation and D&A, and a $57.6M fair-value charge hit on rhode's earnout outperformance. Interest expense nearly tripled to $35.3M on new acquisition debt; tax rate rose to 35% from 23%. Full-year operating income fell to $73.6M from $158.0M; net income fell to $26.3M from $112.1M. Cash rose to $289.7M on $600M of new debt; no dividends or buybacks this quarter. No forward guidance in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Full FY2026 (ended Mar 31, 2026) op income fell 53% y/y and net income fell 76% y/y despite +25% sales, on higher SG&A, a $57.6M rhode earnout fair-value charge, and higher interest expense; the 10-K does not break out this standalone quarter.

FY2026 net sales +25% to $1.64B: the rhode Acquisition (closed Aug 2025) added $293.5M, existing business added $29.5M; higher average item price/mix added $333.5M, partly offset by $10.5M lower volume.
FY2026 gross margin was 70.7%, down ~50bp y/y, driven primarily by tariffs and partly offset by pricing (full fiscal-year disclosure; the 10-K doesn't isolate this quarter).
FY2026 SG&A rose 32% on marketing/distribution, compensation and D&A, and the company booked a $57.6M contingent-consideration fair-value charge tied to rhode's earnout outperformance.
FY2026 interest expense nearly tripled to $35.3M after the Fifth Amendment Term Facility funded the rhode Acquisition, and the effective tax rate rose to 35% from 23%.
Cash rose to $289.7M mainly on $600.0M of new term-loan proceeds and $50.0M of revolver draws used to fund the rhode Acquisition, per the FY2026 financing-activities discussion.
